topic: News breakdown: Microsoft and the AFT's school AI safety and privacy standard, set to apply from Nov 1
post:
Big Tech just made a binding promise not to train AI on student data. 🏫
Here's what's in the Microsoft and teachers' union deal, and why it matters beyond schools.

What happened 👇
🤝 Microsoft, the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) and the United Federation of Teachers announced a "National AI Safety & Privacy Standard" for schools in September
📅 AP reported the standard would apply to schools Microsoft has contracts with starting Nov. 1

What Microsoft committed to 👇
🚫 No using student or educator data to train AI
💸 That data can't be sold or used for advertising
👀 No student tracking, and humans oversee AI decisions
📋 The AFT says it's legally binding, with third-party audits

The catch: districts still have to write the terms into their own contracts. And critics say it only works if every big AI company signs on. OpenAI and Anthropic said they were discussing similar pacts.

Why it matters:
This is what enforceable AI rules can look like: specific promises, audits, and contracts, not just principles. 🔍

Practical takeaway:
If your organization buys AI tools, ask your vendor one question: will our data be used to train your models? Get the answer in writing. 📝

Should every AI company sign a pledge like this? 👇

Follow for daily AI news you can actually use.
